question: When blue and orange lights, which are parallel to each other, are passed through prism then :

options.text: both emergent rays will be parallel
blue ray will bend towards the top

solution:
The correct answer is __**blue ray will bend more**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **splitting of white light into its individual colours** is a process known as **light dispersion**.
 
• The **spectrum **is the **collection of seven colours** that results from the division of white light.
 
• While the **velocities of the individual colours **that make up** white light** are the same in a vacuum, they differ when the light travels through a transparent material like a** glass prism**.
 
• **Different colours are deviated or bent at the prism's first face** at various angles. **Red** has a **minimum angle deviation due to maximum speed** while **violet** has a **maximum angle deviation due to minimum speed**.
 
• When **blue and orange lights, **which are parallel to each other, are passed through a prism, then the **blue ray will bend more** because **blue light has the least wavelength and minimum speed compared to orange light**, so the angle deviation or bending will be more.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **When light rays encounter an obstruction like dust, gas molecules, water vapours, etc., they deviate from their straight-line path**, and this phenomenon is known as the **scattering of light**.
 
• The **"Tyndall effect" and the "red hues of sunrise and sunset"** are just two examples of the phenomena caused by the **scattering of light**.
 
• With an** increase in wavelength, the scattering of light gets less and less**.
 
• The s**ize of the scattering particles affects the colour of the light** that is dispersed.
 
• The **Tyndall effect** is a phenomenon where light is scattered by **colloidal particles**.
